title: AllergenSync: allergen records that follow supplier changes, for restaurants
summary: Restaurants must give correct information on the 14 major allergens, and the UK food regulator now recommends written allergen information for all loose food. The weak point is supplier substitutions. AllergenSync reads supplier spec sheets and invoices, keeps each dish's allergen matrix up to date and warns the kitchen when a substitute changes an allergen.
hook: "The wholesaler sent a different brand of pesto. Nobody checked the label. It had cashews."
story:
**Tom runs two neighbourhood restaurants in Bristol with a menu that changes every season.** His allergen matrix is a laminated A4 sheet made last spring. Since then the wholesaler has **swapped five products** when items were out of stock, and the kitchen has changed three recipes. Nobody updated the sheet, because finding the spec sheet for each product takes an evening.

One Friday a server tells a guest with a nut allergy that the pesto pasta is safe. The substitute pesto contains **cashew nuts**. The guest notices a reaction early and nobody is badly hurt, but Tom gets a visit from the council's food officer and realises his records would not survive a serious case. He needs something that notices product changes for him, not another spreadsheet.
whyNow: The FSA published best-practice guidance in March 2025 saying written allergen information should always be available for non-prepacked food. FSA incidents rose 14% in 2025/26, with allergen incidents rising fastest. AI can now read supplier spec sheets and invoice lines cheaply, which makes automatic change detection possible.
evidence: FSA guidance (March 2025): written allergen information should always be available for non-prepacked food, plus a conversation with the customer [FSA]
FSA incidents rose from 1,825 to 2,073 in 2025/26 (+14%); allergen incidents rose faster than any other category [Food Management Today]
The FSA handled 242 allergen-related incidents and issued 58 allergen alerts in the 2025 period [Food Manufacture]
A consultancy analysis says 597 of 1,036 UK food alerts in 2016–2021 (57.6%) were about allergens; primary source not confirmed [Human Focus]
Kafoodle starts around £20/month per feature; its restaurant bundle is listed from £60/month plus setup [Software Advice / FitGap]

whyReal.title: The stakes are life and death
whyReal.text: Allergen mistakes can kill, and owners know the famous UK cases. Allergen incidents are the fastest-growing type of FSA incident.

whyReal.title: Substitutions break the paperwork
whyReal.text: Most allergen sheets are correct on the day they are made. They go wrong when a supplier swaps a product or the chef changes a recipe, and nobody updates the sheet.

whyReal.title: The regulator raised expectations
whyReal.text: The FSA now recommends written allergen information for all loose food. Councils check allergen controls during hygiene inspections.

whyReal.title: Existing tools are built around recipes, not change
whyReal.text: Recipe and nutrition tools ask the chef to keep everything updated by hand. Few watch incoming invoices and spec sheets for changes.

whoPays.label: Customer
whoPays.text: independent restaurants, cafés, pubs with food, small hotel kitchens and caterers with 1–10 sites.

whoPays.label: Buyer
whoPays.text: owner, head chef or operations manager of a small group.

whoPays.label: Start market
whoPays.text: UK and Ireland in English (same 14 allergens as EU law), then the Nordics and the rest of the EU.

solution.title: Import the menu
solution.text: upload the current menu and recipes (photo, PDF or spreadsheet); AI drafts the ingredient list for each dish.

solution.title: Match the products
solution.text: upload supplier spec sheets or product photos; AI reads the allergens and "may contain" lines and links each product to dishes.

solution.title: Watch for changes
solution.text: forward supplier invoices and delivery notes; when a product code or brand changes, AllergenSync asks for the new spec sheet and recalculates.

solution.title: Warn the team
solution.text: if a dish's allergens change, the chef gets an alert and must approve before the matrix updates.

solution.title: Publish
solution.text: printable allergen matrix, staff tablet view and a QR menu page for guests, all with a change history for inspections.

must: Menu and recipe import with AI ingredient draft
Supplier spec sheet reading (14 allergens + may contain)
Invoice forwarding and product change detection
Printable matrix and QR guest page
later: Staff allergen training quiz and records

techStack: LLM + OCR for spec sheets and invoices

timeline.what: **Validate, no code.** Visit 15 restaurants. Build 3 allergen matrices by hand with Claude from their real spec sheets and invoices.
Menu import, spec sheet reading, matrix and approval flow.
Invoice forwarding, change detection, printable matrix and QR page.

risks.risk: Liability if AI reads a label wrong
risks.answer: AI drafts, the chef approves; every allergen links to the source document; terms make the business responsible for final checks.

risks.risk: Restaurants hate admin and churn fast
risks.answer: Make invoice forwarding the only habit; price low; sell to small groups where one manager covers many sites.
Do not compete on costing or nutrition; own the "supplier change" problem and integrate later.

risks.risk: Spec sheets are hard to get
risks.answer: Accept product photos of the label as a fallback; build a shared product library across customers over time.
